newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-FOMC speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-FOMC speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 40 basis points in early trade on Tuesday at 18.60 percent on speculation ahead of news from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"The FOMC meeting has sparked some speculation. I personally am betting the Fed won't raise U.S. rates, but opinions are divided and the market is waiting to see what happens," a dealer said.
The FOMC is expected to report on its decision at 1315 local time/1815 GMT.
Dealers said that despite early pressure they expected secondary rates to remain within a narrow trading range as volume was thin.
Fixed-income analysts said the FOMC would have no direct effect on the central bank's weekly primary auction of government securities, because bids had to be placed before any decision was expected.
"Jitters ahead of the FOMC could have an impact on auction results, but once the decision is known it will be too late to change bids," one analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper were up 20 basis points at 19.70 percent in early trade.
Liquidity of 136 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
